source_review.notes: Checked current official Apache Flink checkpointing, large-state, configuration, and savepoint documentation; Apache Spark configuration, scheduling, and RDD documentation; Kubernetes Job and disruption documentation; Google Cloud Dataflow workflow guidance; Apache Airflow DAG-run documentation; and Apache Iceberg reliability documentation. All twelve final references returned HTTP 200. Runtime-specific recovery behavior is attributed.

evidence: Reviewed recovery DAG, vertices/dependencies/artifacts/completed boundaries/semantic digests, selected cut, recompute closure, work/amplification, checkpoint cost/interval, assumed failure rate, recovery-stage times, and retention horizons.
Checked end-to-end recovery-time sum and checkpoint-overhead derivative with units and explicit restrictive assumptions.
Checked that useful work, invalidated/repeated work, checkpoint duration, interval, restore time, replay time, RPO, RTO, and completion deadline remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The economic approximation is presented as a reasoning aid constrained by correctness and hard objectives, not as a universal scheduler formula.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced 16.0-hour total runtime, selected 6-hour join checkpoint, 4.0 work-hours RPO, 6.5-hour recovery, 9.5 hours saved, 8.0-hour target, and true RTO attainment.
Recomputed recovery as 0.5 restore + (10 - 6) remaining join + 2 publish = 6.5 hours and savings as 16 - 6.5 = 9.5 hours.
Checked the 350-minute staged RTO example sums 20 + 90 + 30 + 180 + 20 + 10 and the 14-day checkpoint/3-day source example yields at most a 3-day complete horizon.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No universal task size, checkpoint interval, retention, retry count, speculation threshold, failure rate, or RPO/RTO is prescribed.

evidence: Verified compatible dependency-closed boundary selection plus topological descendant recomputation reconstructs the declared target without mixed lineage.
Verified private attempt output and conditional one-winner manifest/transaction make retry and speculation output-safe.
Differentiated d/c + lambda*c/2 to obtain c*=sqrt(2d/lambda), while confirming every independence, uniformity, constant-cost, no-overlap, and immediate-capacity premise is named.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Correlated failure, variable snapshot/restore cost, discrete stage boundaries, tail capacity, and hard RPO constraints require measurement or richer modeling.

evidence: Reviewed first/last/empty/huge units, narrow/wide/iterative stages, shared dependencies, skew, stragglers, speculation, preemption, and adaptive mappings.

Reviewed worker/node/coordinator/storage/zone/region failure, destination outage, capacity starvation, dependency throttling, poison data, corrupt/latest/missing incremental checkpoint, and source/key/code expiry.
Reviewed lost commit replies, sink unknowns, stale epochs, repeated recovery failure, fallback, cleanup races, cold cache/storage, and old-version restore.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Invalid boundaries and terminal failures are rejected/classified rather than retried indefinitely or mixed with other recovery roots.

evidence: Traced stable logical unit and private attempt identity through inputs, execution, output handles, validation, boundary manifests, recovery closure, and cleanup.
Checked complete durable integrity/compatibility/dependency validation, one semantic lineage, source-state-output alignment, idempotent/transactional commits, coordinator fencing, and resume tokens.
Checked failure-domain labels, checkpoint cadence evidence, failure classification, retry/time/resource/deadline budgets, recovery capacity, retention closure, and practiced fallback restore.
invariant_checking.notes: Process exit, path presence, local copies, retry counts, checkpoint success, or retained metadata cannot substitute for end-to-end recoverability.

evidence: Reviewed recovery-cut correctness, attempt safety, coordinator failover, and checkpoint-economics arguments with explicit durability, immutability, determinism, fencing, and distribution premises.

Checked counterexamples for monolithic tasks, driver-only state, local-only snapshots, early completion, shared final paths, newest-directory selection, indiscriminate retry, and incomplete retention.
Checked drills inject every major failure domain, corrupt the newest checkpoint, constrain cold capacity/dependencies, require fallback, and compare state/output/effects before declaring progress.
proof_review.notes: Boundary validity, semantic equivalence, output uniqueness, RPO, RTO, and full completion are independently verified properties.

evidence: Audited recovery unit, durable boundary, recovery graph, RPO/RTO, restart amplification, checkpoint interval/duration, resume token, salvageable output, drill, and failure-budget terminology.
Confirmed task/stage/job/attempt, lineage/materialization/checkpoint, local/remote durability, retry/resume/recompute/restore, and progress/completion distinctions.
Confirmed transient, worker, capacity, deterministic, data, authorization, dependency, corruption, coordinator, and regional failures produce different actions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Flink, Spark, Kubernetes, Dataflow, Airflow, and Iceberg mechanisms are not presented as identical recovery guarantees.

evidence: Reviewed useful progress/rate, checkpoint/materialization size/cost/age, valid coverage, attempts/failures, retry/backoff, lost/repeated work, amplification, and closure size.
Reviewed election, capacity wait, validation, restore, replay/recompute, commit, verification, fallback, deadline slack, RPO/RTO, and completion latency.

Confirmed segmentation by job/stage/unit/attempt, input size/skew, graph/code/schema version, checkpoint/boundary, failure domain/type, resource pool, dependency/storage, mode, percentile, and window.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Fast state loading, successful checkpoints, average recovery, or task completion is not mislabeled as end-to-end objective attainment.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed objectives, recovery units/graphs, stage boundaries, in-stage checkpoints, atomic manifests, coordinator tokens/fencing, failure classification, budgets, checkpoint economics, capacity, retention, deterministic recovery, stragglers/preemption, completion, drills, and observability.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable logical identities, manifests, checksums, checkpoint contents, coordinator records, classifiers, multidimensional budgets, capacity reservations, dependency-closure retention, ordered recovery, conditional winners, sink reconciliation, dashboards, and regional drills. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from objectives and decomposition through durable progress and economic choices to actual incident recovery and proof. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover monolith decomposition, boundaries, iterative state, local/remote recovery, terminal errors, retention, speculation, staged RTO, fallback, timeout modeling, coordinator state, and regional drills.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Flink/Spark/Kubernetes/Dataflow/Airflow/Iceberg maintainer, distributed-systems/data-platform/scheduler/storage/SRE/security/economics specialist, production long-job operator, downstream consumer, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
